Read Today's Paper Sebi’s CAS guidelines likely within a week, says chief Tuhin Kanta Pandey SECTIONS Sebi’s CAS guidelines likely within a week, says chief Tuhin Kanta Pandey By Kumar Gaurav , ETMarkets.com Last Updated: Oct 10, 2026, 07:28:00 PM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis Sebi chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said the regulator expects to issue guidelines on the settlement-price mechanism for derivatives on expiry days within a week. The move follows a review of the Closing Auction Session. Sebi is also working on simpler regulations, easier market access, lower compliance costs and stronger technological resilience. THE ECONOMIC TIMES The CAS review is part of Sebi’s broader efforts to deepen India’s cash markets, improve price discovery and enhance market efficiency. The Securities and Exchange Board of India ( Sebi ) is likely to issue guidelines on the settlement-price mechanism for derivatives on expiry days within about a week, chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said on Saturday. The regulator is examining feedback on its consultation paper following a review of the Closing Auction Session (CAS). “Following review of the Closing Auction Session, a consultation paper was put out to address concerns in respect of settlement price of derivatives on expiry-day. We are currently examining the comments and hope to issue guidelines in about a week’s time,” Pandey said at the second Capital Market Confluence 2026, organised by the Bombay Stock Exchange Brokers’ Forum in Mumbai. The CAS review is part of Sebi’s broader efforts to deepen India’s cash markets, improve price discovery and enhance market efficiency. Pandey said wider participation, stronger securities borrowing and lending, and efficient hedging and arbitrage could help improve liquidity and the functioning of cash markets. In his address, titled “From Regulation to Global Leadership: Positioning India’s Capital Markets as a Standard-Setter for the Next Decade”, the Sebi chairman outlined four broad priorities for the market regulator: proportionate regulation, deeper cash markets, easier access to Indian markets and greater technological resilience. On the regulatory front, Pandey said Sebi was reviewing the Depositories and Participants Regulations to simplify rules and strengthen fraud prevention. The regulator is also exploring a graded compliance framework for stock brokers based on their scale, client exposure and dependence on technology. Live Events “One size need not fit all,” he said. Sebi is also addressing gaps in the interoperability framework for certain transactions, including tender offers, buybacks and offers for sale (OFS). These transactions currently require parallel clearing arrangements, adding to costs and compliance requirements, Pandey said. The regulator is targeting implementation of the proposed changes by the end of November 2026. The move is expected to improve capital efficiency and lower compliance costs while preserving settlement safety, he said. Legendary value investor Michael Price believed successful investing requires independent thinking, rigorous research and the discipline to look beyond short-term market movements. His investment philosophy focused on identifying companies trading below their intrinsic value , particularly businesses facing temporary financial difficulties that have the potential to recover. Price developed much of his approach under the guidance of veteran investor Max Heine of Mutual Series Mutual Funds. Over the years, he built a reputation for investing in undervalued companies and identifying opportunities that other market participants may overlook. Look beyond cheap valuations Price believed a low share price or an inexpensive valuation does not automatically make a stock an attractive investment. Investors must establish whether a company's intrinsic value is significantly higher than its current market price. Live Events Traditional valuation measures, including the price-to-book and price-to-cash-flow ratios, can help investors assess whether a stock is undervalued. However, these metrics must be considered alongside the company's financial position, competitive strengths, management quality and prospects for recovery. Price's strategy involved examining businesses experiencing financial difficulties to determine whether their underlying operations remained fundamentally sound. If the problems are temporary and the company can recover, its shares may offer an opportunity to buy at a substantial discount to their underlying worth. He also recommended examining individual business segments separately and studying mergers and acquisitions to understand how potential buyers value companies and their assets. Around 14 companies, including Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Vedanta and Ola Electric Mobility , have scheduled record dates for dividends, bonus issues and other corporate actions during the week of October 12 (Monday) to October 16 (Friday). To be eligible for these corporate actions, investors must hold the shares in their demat accounts as of the respective record dates. The list is tentative, as more companies may announce record dates for dividends, bonus issues, stock splits and rights issues during the week. Here is the day-wise list of corporate actions to watch out for this week: October 12 (Monday) Smallcap pharma company Jojo has fixed October 12 (Monday) as the record date for its 1:1 bonus issue. This means that eligible shareholders owning one share of the company with a face value of Rs 5 each on BSE will get one bonus share with the same face value following the corporate action. Live Events October 13 (Tuesday) Ola Electric shares will turn ex-record date for its Rs 1,000 crore rights issue with the issue price being fixed at Rs 27 per share. The electric two-wheeler maker will issue 37.03 crore partly paid-up shares under the offer. The rights issue will open on October 22 and close on October 30. Shareholders can sell or transfer their rights entitlement in the market until October 26. Shareholders will pay Rs 16.20 per share upfront, while the remaining Rs 10.80 will be paid later. The company plans to collect the remaining amount by October 31, 2027, according to exchange filings. Additionally, GIFT City-based fintech company AvenuesAI will also turn ex-record date for consolidation of 10:1. October 14 (Wednesday) Wednesday will account for two high-profile dividend stocks , with the record date being fixed on October 14 (Wednesday). Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) will pay an interim dividend of Rs 12 per share to its eligible shareholders. The IT major last week declared the dividend, while reporting a 15% year-on-year (YoY) rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 13,884 crore for the second quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 12,075 crore in the year-ago period. India's primary market will see at least Rs 1,572 crore worth of IPOs open next week, led by three mainboard issues from HD Fire Protect, Fusion CX and Sahajanand Medical Technologies. The week will be more active on the subscription side than on listings. Three mainboard IPOs and two SME IPOs will open for bidding, while the only listing scheduled is RK Fashion Accessories, whose SME issue was subscribed 2.7 times. HD Fire Protect IPO HD Fire Protect will open its Rs 712 crore IPO on October 13 and close it on October 15. The issue is entirely an offer for sale of 2.63 crore shares, which means the company will not receive any money from the IPO. The price band has been fixed at Rs 258-271 per share, with a lot size of 55 shares. At the upper end, the company will command a market capitalisation of about Rs 4,749 crore. The stock is expected to list on October 21. Incorporated in 1997, HD Fire Protect manufactures and supplies fire protection equipment and systems. Its products include sprinklers, alarm valves, deluge valves, foam systems, monitors, nozzles, custom-engineered systems and gas suppression systems. The company caters to oil and gas, refining, petrochemicals, power, heavy engineering, aerospace, pharmaceuticals, data centres, hospitality and healthcare. HD Fire Protect has exported to more than 90 countries since inception and operates two manufacturing facilities in Maharashtra. Its revenue rose from Rs 372.95 crore in FY24 to Rs 489.28 crore in FY26, while profit after tax stood at Rs 116.79 crore in FY26, against Rs 109.72 crore a year earlier. Live Events Fusion CX IPO Fusion CX will open its Rs 702 crore IPO on October 14 and close it on October 16. The issue includes a fresh issue of Rs 500 crore and an offer for sale of Rs 202 crore. The price band has been fixed at Rs 275-289 per share, with a lot size of 51 shares. At the upper end, the company’s market cap will be around Rs 4,172 crore. The stock is expected to list on October 22. Fusion CX is a customer experience and business process solutions provider.
